snip.s: Childhood Asthma: Clinical Features, Diagnosis and Management

qs.q: An 11-year-old girl with known asthma undergoes routine monitoring while asymptomatic. Spirometry is within normal limits, but her fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is markedly elevated. What does this finding primarily indicate?
o: Presence of active bacterial pulmonary infection
Development of fixed structural airway remodeling
Evidence of poor patient inhalation technique
Presence of active eosinophilic airway inflammation
qs.e: Elevated fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a specific biomarker reflecting type-2 eosinophilic airway inflammation in patients with asthma. Normal spirometry when asymptomatic does not rule out underlying ongoing airway inflammation.
qs.s: Childhood Asthma: Clinical Features, Diagnosis and Management: MCQs

qs.q: A clinician reviewing diagnostic biomarkers for a patient with suspected asthma notes a raised FeNO level of 55 ppb. What specific pathological process does this elevated fraction of exhaled nitric oxide reflect?
qs.e: A raised FeNO level greater than 40-50 ppb supports eosinophilic inflammation in asthma phenotypes. It does not measure fixed fibrosis or bacterial bronchitis.
qs.s: Bronchial Asthma: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and GINA Stepwise: MCQs
